short: Expected cost along branches and loops

lean.name: ResourceCounting.expectedCost
lean.plain: Resource charges weighted by branch probability
lean.annotation: The `qAssign` case multiplies `model.unitaryCost unitary` by `state.trace`, the mass the paper calls `stateMass`. In a search that always makes one oracle call and makes a second only on an outcome of probability $1/4$, the two calls contribute $1$ and $1/4$ rounds respectively.

lean.name: ResourceCounting.CostBound.qWhile
lean.plain: Expected iteration count times the body cost bound
lean.annotation: `activeIter` at index $j$ is the state entering iteration $j+1$. Its trace is the mass charged for that iteration. A body cost bound $B$ gives a charge of at most $B$ times that trace. The bound `iterations` is measured per unit of input trace, so a loop starting at trace $t$ costs at most $t\,\mathtt{iterations}\,B$.

lean.name: ResourceCounting.expectedCost
lean.plain: Resource charges weighted by branch probability
lean.annotation: The `qIf` case adds the costs on the two restricted states. If only one branch runs four $T$ gates and that branch has mass $1/2$, the conditional contributes two gates in expectation with unit $T$ weights. For a loop, the `qWhile` case takes the supremum over finite unrolling costs.

statements.markdown: semantic expected-cost accounting over program executions with branching and unbounded loops
